sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 16:272

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 16:272:1
items.html: The existence of the seven kings under every discernment, in Bina, in ZA, and in Malchut. The principal discernment is the anterior vessels — GE in the Rosh [head] and HGT up to the Chazeh [chest] in the Guf [body] — and under them are the posterior vessels, which are half of Bina, and ZA and Malchut, both in the Rosh and in the Guf, and they are regarded as the seven kings, which are ZAT.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 16:272:2
items.html: And at the Sium of each of them, and in their three lower ones, in the posterior, for this is called “under”: The half of Bina, and ZA and Malchut of the Guf [body] and Rosh [head], are called by all these names: the seven kings, ZAT, Sium, the three lower ones, posterior, and “under.” And opposite them, the anterior vessels are called the principal discernment, and are called GAR or the seven first ones.
